result.conclusion: No — the current intake does not collect all facts needed for a defensible preliminary eligibility conclusion for every pathway you attempt to cover. It supports high‑level triage (flags, rough prioritization) and allows some preliminary MSP screening because CMS permits self‑attestation for certain items, but important, program‑determinative facts are missing (Medicare Part A/B status, citizenship/declaration, precise income and ownership by household member, asset values including life insurance cash value and burial funds, household composition/eligibility unit, and authoritative VA/California/SSA references). Below are focused screening gaps (<=12) that, if resolved in intake or immediate follow‑up, would allow a defensible preliminary eligibility determination for the pathways you actually screen (MSPs, full‑benefit Medicaid/Medi‑Cal, VA caregiver/pension triage, SSDI/SSI triage).

screening_gaps.criterion: Medicare Part A and/or Part B enrollment (which part(s) are active)
screening_gaps.pathway: Medicare Savings Programs (QMB/SLMB/QI) and LIS-related routing
missing_facts: Whether recipient has Medicare Part A and/or Part B (Part A enrollment can be dispositive for LIS/MSP pathways)
If unknown, a clear 'I'm not sure' option is present but intake lacks a targeted follow‑up question to resolve it
screening_gaps.trigger: case.goals includes 'Medical coverage' or recipient.health_coverage includes 'Medicare' or intake attempts MSP screening
simple_questions: Does [recipient name] have Medicare Part A (hospital) and/or Part B (medical)? (Choose 'Part A only', 'Part B only', 'Both A & B', 'No Medicare', 'I'm not sure')
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If user answers 'I'm not sure' or if MSP eligibility appears near a threshold — look up SSA/Medicare enrollment or request Medicare card at application.
screening_gaps.caveat: For preliminary screening self‑report is permissible, but agency verification will occur at application.

screening_gaps.criterion: U.S. citizenship or satisfactory immigration status and signed declaration
screening_gaps.pathway: MSPs and Medicaid/full‑benefit Medicaid (including state MSPs)
missing_facts: Self‑reported citizenship/immigration status (citizen, U.S. national, satisfactory immigration status, or not)
Whether the applicant will complete the signed declaration required by states
screening_gaps.trigger: Any screening for MSPs or state Medicaid, or when case.goals includes 'Medical coverage'
simple_questions: Is [recipient name] a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or a non‑citizen with satisfactory immigration status? (Yes / No / I'm not sure)
Will they be able to sign the state declaration of citizenship/immigration status if needed? (Yes / No / I'm not sure)
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If non‑citizen or 'I'm not sure' — lookup state requirements and identify which immigration documents will be required at application.

screening_gaps.criterion: Precise monthly income amounts and ownership by household member (gross/net) and spouse income
missing_facts: Exact gross monthly income (recipient and spouse/partner), and which household members contribute income
Breakdown by income source (SSA, wages, pension, VA, interest/dividends)
screening_gaps.trigger: recipient.monthly_income_range not 'No income' OR case.goals includes MSP/Medical coverage OR income range is near MSP thresholds
simple_questions: Please enter gross monthly income for [recipient name], and for spouse/partner if applicable; specify the source for each amount (Social Security, wages, pension, VA, other).
Which household members contribute income and are included in the Medicaid/MSP household?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If amounts are near state thresholds or intake must make a defensible conclusion — request paystubs/SSA award letters or perform state threshold lookup before final recommendation.
screening_gaps.caveat: CMS allows self‑attestation for some items, but precise dollar amounts and household composition are necessary to place someone reliably into a specific MSP band for a defensible preliminary conclusion.

screening_gaps.criterion: Household composition and eligibility unit (names/ages/relationships/tax dependency)
screening_gaps.pathway: MSPs and Medicaid household size rules (family size can change MSP banding)
missing_facts: List of household members with relationship to recipient and ages
Which household members are claimed as tax dependents or contribute income (affects eligibility unit)
screening_gaps.trigger: When computing FPL percentage for MSPs or when household size could change eligibility band
simple_questions: List everyone who lives in the household with [recipient name], their relationship, and ages (include whether each contributes income or is claimed on taxes).
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If household composition is ambiguous or unusual (e.g., non‑spouse adult relatives), lookup state/memo guidance (see CMS memo referenced in Chapter 1) or request tax returns at application.
screening_gaps.caveat: Family-size rules can be state‑sensitive; ask explicitly about tax dependency and income ownership to compute the correct eligibility unit.

screening_gaps.criterion: Countable resources: approximate current values, life insurance cash value, and burial funds (owner & dates)
current_fields: recipient.assets (types only: primary home, other property, savings/investments, None, I'm not sure)
missing_facts: Approximate current values for savings, investment account balances, cash value of life insurance, burial funds (and whether burial funds are in a separate account), and ownership (recipient or spouse)
Whether assets have been transferred and when (if relevant to resource calculation)
screening_gaps.trigger: recipient.assets includes any asset types other than 'None' OR case.goals includes MSP/Medicaid long‑term care
simple_questions: For each asset type selected, please provide an approximate current value and who owns it (recipient, spouse, other).
Does the life insurance policy have a cash surrender value? If yes, approximate amount.
Are burial funds in a separate account or commingled?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If values approach resource limits, or state uses AVS — request bank statements, life insurance statements, property valuations at application or perform AVS lookup if allowed.
screening_gaps.caveat: CMS requires states to accept self‑attestation for interest/dividends and some non‑liquid resources but states may use AVS or request verification; ask values to judge likely countability and whether verification will be requested.

screening_gaps.criterion: State of residence tied to state MSP names, thresholds, and verification rules
missing_facts: Explicit mapping from the recipient's state to the state MSP program name, state thresholds, and whether the state uses AVS or additional verification beyond CMS guidance
screening_gaps.trigger: case.goals includes 'Medical coverage' or interest in help paying Medicare
simple_questions: Confirm the recipient's state of residence for benefit lookup (if different from caregiver). Would you like us to look up the state's MSP name and income/resource thresholds now?
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: Always: when preparing to recommend applying or to determine exact MSP thresholds and verification requirements, perform a state MSP lookup.
screening_gaps.caveat: State differences are material — intake must either collect the state and trigger a lookup or embed a state‑specific threshold table in screening logic.

screening_gaps.criterion: Asset transfers / lookback (dates, amounts, recipients) relevant to Medi‑Cal long‑term care eligibility
screening_gaps.pathway: Medi‑Cal long‑term services (including IHSS referral and nursing home eligibility) — transfer penalty rules
current_fields: recipient.recent_transfers (asked only when living_setting == 'Nursing home or skilled nursing facility')
missing_facts: Whether any transfers occurred in the state lookback period (date of transfer, amount, who received the transfer, reason)
Transfers outside nursing home context (transfers can also affect other long‑term care eligibility)
screening_gaps.trigger: recipient.living_setting indicates nursing home or case.goals includes long‑term care/Medi‑Cal help; also trigger when applicant requests IHSS or other Medi‑Cal long‑term services
simple_questions: Have any assets or property been transferred, sold for less than fair market value, or given away in the last 30 months? If yes, list dates, amounts, and recipients.
If transfers occurred more than 30 months ago, please state dates and amounts.
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If any transfers are reported or suspected, collect transaction records, deeds, or other proofs at application and lookup California Medi‑Cal IHSS transfer/lookback rules if the resident is in CA.
screening_gaps.caveat: This is jurisdiction‑sensitive (California rules differ and the team did not retrieve CA IHSS/Medi‑Cal sources). Marked as a visibility gap; authoritative state docs required to complete this criterion.

screening_gaps.criterion: VA evidence and caregiver relationship / coresidence for VA pension/Aid & Attendance and PCAFC caregiver pathways
screening_gaps.pathway: VA pension (Aid & Attendance) and VA caregiver programs (PCAFC)
missing_facts: VA decision or award letter (combined rating, pension/Aid & Attendance award)
VA claim/file number (application‑only acceptable to collect later)
Precise evidence of caregiver coresidence/relationship when required by PCAFC (if pursuing PCAFC) and whether caregiver is the primary in‑home provider
screening_gaps.trigger: case.goals includes 'Finding VA caregiver benefits' or recipient.current_benefits includes VA pension/aid & attendance
simple_questions: Do you have the VA decision letter or pension/Aid & Attendance award letter? (Yes / No / I'm not sure)
Does the caregiver live with the veteran and provide primary, continuous personal care? (Yes / No / I'm not sure)
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If applying or making a firm eligibility determination, request VA decision/award letters and look up the specific VA program eligibility rules (VBA/VHA guidance).
screening_gaps.caveat: Authoritative VA source documents were not retrieved in the prior audit — this gap prevents defensible VA pathway conclusions and must be resolved with VA regulations/decision letters.

screening_gaps.criterion: Detailed SSA work credits and medical evidence timing needed to triage SSDI eligibility
screening_gaps.pathway: SSDI (work credits) and SSI (income/resources + disability) triage
current_fields: recipient.work_history_social_security (coarse: 'Yes, for several years' / 'Yes, but briefly' / 'No')
missing_facts: Number of quarters of coverage / years in which Social Security taxes were paid (or clear statement that SSA earnings record can be accessed)
Whether medical documentation exists and approximate dates for onset (needed for medical CDR timing)
screening_gaps.trigger: case.goals includes 'Getting SSI, SSDI' or recipient.condition_limits_work == 'Yes'
simple_questions: List the years you worked and indicate whether Social Security taxes were paid in those years (or say if you can get your SSA earnings record).
Is there a medical record or physician who can document disability onset and severity? (Yes / No / I'm not sure)
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: If pursuing SSDI/SSI application or making a preliminary close call, check SSA guidance/POMS for quarters of coverage and obtain SSA earnings record or W‑2s at application.
screening_gaps.caveat: SSA authoritative sources (POMS/regulations) were not retrieved in the prior audit — treat SSDI/SSI triage as provisional until those sources are consulted or the applicant provides SSA award/earnings records.

screening_gaps.criterion: Verification method (AVS vs. self‑attestation) and whether state will use AVS for reported assets/income
screening_gaps.pathway: MSP verification process and potential documentary requests
missing_facts: Whether the recipient's state accepts self‑attestation for non‑liquid resources and interest/dividend income, or whether the state will use AVS and thus may request documentation
If AVS will be used, which accounts/resources are covered by AVS (bank accounts, life insurance, etc.)
screening_gaps.trigger: Any reported assets or when case.goals includes MSPs/Medical coverage
simple_questions: Would you like us to check whether your state accepts self‑attestation for assets or uses AVS verification? (Yes / No)
If you prefer, provide permission to attempt AVS lookup (application stage) — otherwise, please provide approximate asset values now.
screening_gaps.document_lookup_when: Perform a state policy lookup for AVS use and request documents only if AVS fails or state requires evidence.
screening_gaps.caveat: CMS requires states to implement simplifications but states have until specific implementation timelines and may vary in practice.

application_only: Collect signed citizenship/immigration declaration and immigration documents (if non‑citizen) — application stage mandatory (CMS-MSP-CHAPTER-1:30:2889d87192).
Request Medicare card or SSA/Medicare enrollment evidence if needed for agency verification (application stage).
Request SSA award letters (SSI/SSDI) and SSA earnings record or W‑2s/1099s to confirm SSDI work credits (application stage).
Gather bank statements, life insurance policy statements (cash surrender values), and property deeds/valuations when assets approach state resource limits (application).
Obtain VA decision/award letters and VA claim/file numbers if pursuing VA pension/Aid & Attendance or PCAFC (application stage).
Collect documentation of any asset transfers (deeds, transaction records) when transfers may trigger Medi‑Cal lookback penalties (application stage).
Do not request SSNs, account numbers, or BIC routing numbers in screening; collect those only through secure application processes as required by the agency.
visibility_gaps: Authoritative VA policy/regulatory sources (VBA/VHA guidance and eligibility regs) were not retrieved in the prior audit — needed to map exact VA thresholds and caregiver relationship/coresidence requirements.

California-specific Medi‑Cal/IHSS transfer/lookback, asset treatment, and long‑term care eligibility rules were not retrieved — intake cannot produce a defensible CA Medi‑Cal long‑term care conclusion without these.

SSA authoritative guidance (POMS/regulations) on quarters of coverage, SSDI technical work‑credit calculations, and SSI resource rules were not retrieved — intake lacks the source basis to compute SSDI likelihood from coarse work history.
unsupported_or_stale_claims: Prior audit entries referring to VA thresholds and CA IHSS/Medi‑Cal transfer rules were recorded but no authoritative VA or California state documents were retrieved to support those mappings (see the '(NOT RETRIEVED)' items in prior audit). Treat VA/CA claims as unverified until authoritative sources are added.

The intake assumes self‑attestation is broadly sufficient for preliminary MSP screening — this is supported by CMS for many items, but the state‑by‑state verification practice (AVS use) can change the documentary burden; rely on CMS-MSP-CHAPTER-1 sections but confirm state practice.
scope_limits: This audit addresses only whether intake collects facts required to form a defensible preliminary eligibility conclusion, not whether an application is ready or should be approved.

Asset rules and transfer‑penalty calculations are date‑sensitive and jurisdiction‑sensitive; for any historical assets/transfers the audit flags the need for documentary review and authoritative state rules (e.g., California Medi‑Cal).

Self‑report is acceptable for many preliminary MSP screening items per CMS — but a defensible preliminary conclusion that a person will be approved by the agency requires precise income, asset values, household composition, and sometimes documentary evidence; intake must collect these facts or trigger an immediate lookup.
This audit does not compute eligibility or produce binary determinations — it identifies what specific missing facts prevent defensible preliminary conclusions across the covered pathways.
